result.title: CalVLA: Shaping Native Confidence in Vision-Language-Action Policies with Outcome Supervision
result.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the Science of Physical AI Safety (SPAIS) Workshop, CoRL 2026
result.summary: Can a vision-language-action (VLA) policy signal likely task failure from its own action probabilities? We introduce CalVLA, which shapes native action-token confidence using successful and failed rollouts and an Action-Confidence Alignment (ACal) squared margin-ranking loss. Low-rank adapters update OpenVLA-7B without an auxiliary failure detector. Observations are paired within tasks at similar normalized elapsed times, not necessarily equivalent physical progress. On a held-out test split from 500 LIBERO-10 configurations, adapted confidence achieves a joint failure-discrimination AUROC of $0.7392\pm0.0480$ over three seeds, averaging scores at 130 and 260 steps. Frozen-policy probes reach 0.6146--0.6436, but superiority over the linear probe is statistically inconclusive. For the same confidence summary, AUROC rises from 0.4485 before adaptation to 0.7327 after adaptation. Mean task success decreases from 58% to 55%. These results show improved failure discrimination, not improved control or established safety benefits.

AI.brief_summary: CalVLA 用成功/失败轨迹和平方 margin-ranking 损失（ACal），以 LoRA 调整 OpenVLA-7B 的 action-token 置信度，使策略自身概率可用于判别任务失败，而无需外挂失败检测器；在 LIBERO-10 留出集上把失败判别 AUROC 从约 0.45 提升到 0.73，同时任务成功率由 58% 降至 55%。
AI.relevance_reason: 以结果监督塑造内部置信度读数，与 LVR 中「是否该停止/验证」及内部状态是否可信的判读问题可能相通；但其对象是 VLA 动作 token 而非 latent 推理状态，且置信度提升未带来控制收益，可供核查「置信/证据信号与行为改进的贡献分配」这一隐患。
